questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Rent seeking as a resource cost
questions.learningObjective: Identify rent seeking as a resource cost
questions.stem: In an engineer's design brief for a bridge, lobbying for a monopoly license consumes real resources without creating new value; this is best described as:

options.text: A resource cost that dissipates potential surplus
A transfer payment with no social cost
options.misconception: ignores the resources consumed by rent seeking

options.text: A productive investment that raises total surplus
options.misconception: confuses rent seeking with value-creating investment

options.text: A price ceiling that helps consumers
options.misconception: mislabels rent seeking as a price control

questions.explanation: Rent seeking uses resources to capture transfers rather than create value, so it is a real social cost. The tempting idea that it is only a transfer ignores the dissipated resources.
questions.hint: Rent seeking consumes resources to redistribute surplus.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Two effects of a per-unit tax
questions.learningObjective: State the two effects of a per-unit tax
questions.stem: A per-unit tax on concrete in the design brief raises revenue and also:

options.text: Has no effect on quantity traded
options.misconception: ignores the quantity distortion from a tax

options.text: Reduces the quantity traded below the efficient level

questions.explanation: A per-unit tax lowers quantity traded below the efficient level, creating deadweight loss, while raising revenue. The tempting idea that revenue is the only effect ignores quantity distortion.
questions.hint: Taxes raise revenue but reduce quantity.

questions.learningObjective: Determine which side to tax for efficiency

confuses who pays with who bears the burden

options.text: Whichever side is less elastic, to minimize distortion
The side whose action creates the externality

questions.explanation: The tax should target the activity causing the externality, regardless of statutory incidence. The tempting idea that elasticity determines which side to tax confuses burden with targeting.

questions.stem: Explain why the statutory side of a corrective tax does not determine who ultimately bears its burden.
